summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail.
takeaways: In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks.

Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.
However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail.
